headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded content and browse live web, while Airflow can emit broad networked automation outputs that may be treated as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no direct shared channel in the profiles, but B can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context while A can produce automation outputs that may be copied into B manually. That makes prompt injection plausible only through unusual operator bridging, with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator copies Airflow-generated text into Perplexity prompts or uploads Airflow outputs as documents, injection becomes possible.
IF no manual transfer or shared workspace exists, this pathway remains blocked.
mitigations: Keep Airflow outputs out of Perplexity prompts unless reviewed.
Use a fixed template for pasted content and strip instructions.
Mark uploaded files as data-only before analysis.
Separate operator workflows for orchestration and search.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared sensitive data classes and B only handles search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context. There is no shared filesystem or OAuth principal in the profiles, so leakage is limited to operator-uploaded content rather than an inherent pairwise data path.
conditions: IF the operator uploads confidential files into Perplexity, those contents enter B's browsing context.
IF Airflow is used to generate or move sensitive data into uploaded documents, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or regulated data to Perplexity.
Redact documents before analysis.
Use separate accounts for orchestration and search.
Review Airflow task outputs before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress but no filesystem write or git mutation; B has vendor-only egress and no shell, filesystem write, or git state changes. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so conflict is limited to coordination mistakes rather than direct resource contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or SaaS resource, they can still race on that shared resource.
IF an orchestrator grants additional write scopes not listed here, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct API keys per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same SaaS object.
Serialize any shared-resource updates.
Monitor for duplicate actions.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's search-and-citation workflow can treat A-produced text as input, and A can emit broad networked outputs that may be copied into B without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so erroneous Airflow output can cascade into Perplexity answers or citations.
conditions: IF Airflow output is pasted into Perplexity as source material, B may amplify errors.
IF Perplexity is used to summarize or cite Airflow-generated claims without independent checking, cascading error occurs.
mitigations: Verify Airflow outputs before sharing.
Require source links for any claim copied into Perplexity.
Use Perplexity only for retrieval, not authority.
Cross-check critical facts against primary sources.
requires-engineering: add citation provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: A is source-available Apache Airflow with no declared data classes, while B is vendor-hosted Perplexity handling search queries and uploaded documents. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is explicit in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen uploads rather than an inherent breach.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated documents are uploaded into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may apply.
IF Airflow is used to route regulated data into B, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data to Perplexity.
Check retention settings before use.
Use anonymized samples for analysis.
Keep Airflow pipelines away from regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and residency review.
